title: High tea after street heat: What happened at INDIA bloc meet at Rahul Gandhi's residence
text:
INDIA bloc leaders gathered at Rahul's residence for high tea after four days of protest on streets

NEW DELHI: INDIA bloc leaders gathered at Rahul Gandhi's residence on Tuesday for high tea amid their ongoing protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged vote theft. They met for a high tea after four days of protest and filing a petition in SC against the CEC. From directly slamming the CEC to criticising the SIR process and criticising PM Modi and Amit Shah, several leaders including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Supriya Sule, Tejashwi Yadav, Sanjay Raut addressed a press conference after the meet vowing to continue their protests while giving insights into what they decided at the meeting. Here's what some of the key leaders saidRahul Gandhi (Congress) Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi anonunced that the INDIA bloc would continue its fight to restore the democratic process and ensure accountability for those he accused of undermining it. "We are all standing here together as one. As I said yesterday, there are no parallel protests. There is one singular protest, and the protest has one mission: restoration of democracy in India. Democracy has been destroyed in this country. The election system has been destroyed. The Constitution has been torn up and thrown away. We are fighting together to restore democratic rule, genuine democratic rule in this country." He thanked people who supported the protest and vowed to bring those responsible to justice. "It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice." "Yesterday, you saw an expression not of the political party standing here, but an expression of the people of India...We would like to thank the people of Delhi, the people of India, who stood with us against what is being done. This is not about us. This is about the people of India. This is about the future of the people of India, and we, all of us together, because we love you and we respect you, are going to fight to the end to restore the democratic process in this country. It is our commitment to you that the people who have done this, Mr. Modi, Mr. Shah, Mr. Gyanesh Kumar, the lady who's hiding right now in Dehradun, and others are going to be brought to justice," he added. Further assuring the work of the team, the Congress leader said, "I used the word 'perseverance' at the press conference yesterdayâ€”that this team of ours is not going to stop. title: 'Donâ€™t post videos': Embassy issues fresh advisory for Indians in Saudi
text:
The fresh advisories come after an October 10 attack on Riyadh airport killed an Indian national

NEW DELHI: Indian embassies in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday issued fresh advisories for Indian nationals amid flight disruptions following the suspension of services by Indian airlines to several Saudi cities until October 17. The Indian Embassy in Riyadh advised Indian nationals to remain calm and vigilant, stay indoors in the event of an aerial attack and follow instructions issued by local authorities through official channels. It also urged Indians to refrain from circulating or reposting videos or news related to the ongoing events. The Embassy said Air India and Air India Express had suspended flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah until October 17. Akasa Air suspended services to and from Riyadh and Jeddah, while IndiGo cancelled flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah and Medina until the same date. The General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) has announced the suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh. Operations at other major airports, including Dammam, Jeddah and Medina, are continuing, although disruptions have been reported. The Embassy advised Indian nationals to remain in regular contact with their respective airlines and verify the latest status of their flights. Those needing to leave Saudi Arabia in an emergency may also consider flights from neighbouring Gulf countries, particularly Qatar and Bahrain, subject to obtaining the required visas. The Consulate General of India in Jeddah issued a separate advisory, particularly for Umrah pilgrims travelling to and from Jeddah and Medina. It urged passengers to check with airlines before proceeding to airports and remain in contact with travel agents, tour operators and Umrah service providers regarding cancellations, rescheduling, alternative travel arrangements and accommodation. The Consulate said it was in regular contact with airlines and local authorities to assist affected Indian nationals. Both the Embassy in Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah have established 24x7 control rooms to provide assistance. The Riyadh Embassy also said Indian nationals who arrived in Saudi Arabia on visit, tourist, Umrah or business visas but were forced to overstay because of flight unavailability would be allowed to leave without paying fines. Those whose visas have expired were advised to exit the Kingdom as soon as flights become available. title: Ashwin reveals what drove Bhuvneshwar's India comeback
text:
Bhuvneshwar Kumar

Ravichandran Ashwin believes Bhuvneshwar Kumar's return to India's T20I setup is a reward for his consistency rather than the result of chasing an international comeback. The veteran pacer earned a recall to the national squad after impressing for Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) in the IPL, with Ashwin crediting his focus on performance for his return. Bhuvneshwar's selection for India's upcoming five-match T20I series against New Zealand, beginning next week, was one of the major talking points following the squad announcement. The right-arm pacer is set to return to international T20 cricket after a gap of four years.

'He has gone on his own journey'

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Ashwin suggested that Bhuvneshwar remained focused on improving his bowling and fulfilling his responsibilities for RCB rather than worrying about a potential India recall. "I have a feeling that Bhuvneshwar Kumar hasn't even thought about a comeback. I think this will be his mantra for success. And when I'm watching him from afar, I have also experienced this myself, he has gone on his own journey," Ashwin said. "He has focused on doing well, bowling well with the new ball and performing for RCB. Whatever he could do, he did it. His recall is the reward for his success. He never chased that reward; he simply did his job and success followed," he added.

Ashwin backs India for 2027 ODI World Cup, picks South Africa as serious contenders

Looking ahead to the 2027 ODI World Cup, Ashwin backed India to challenge for the title but warned that hosts South Africa could pose a significant threat in familiar conditions. Ashwin pointed to India's pace-bowling resources, spin options and batting experience as reasons to believe the team can mount a strong campaign. He particularly highlighted Bumrah's importance, suggesting that the fast bowler could make a major difference if he performs at his best. "India has the ability. If Jasprit Bumrah is firing on all cylinders, he will have a good fast-bowling experience. India has a good spin stock. There, in a lot of grounds, you will get the help of spin. There is experience in batting," he said. However, Ashwin identified South Africa as one of the strongest contenders, citing home advantage, familiarity with local conditions and the experience players have gained through the SA20 league.

title: Delhi man with 14 criminal cases shot dead, CCTV captures killing
text:
The deceased, identified as Mosin Khan, was a resident of Commander Chowk in Vikas Nagar.

NEW DELHI: A man with around 14 criminal cases registered against him was shot dead in a brazen attack captured on CCTV in outer Delhiâ€™s Ranhola area, police said on Tuesday. The footage shows the victim stopping his motorcycle near a house when two motorcycles carrying four assailants suddenly enter the camera frame. The attackers approach the rider, and one of them opens fire from behind. The other assailants also fire multiple shots at the victim before the attack unfolds in full view of the CCTV camera. The deceased, identified as Mosin Khan, was a resident of Commander Chowk in Vikas Nagar and a declared bad character (BC) of Ranhola police station, according to police. Police said they received information around 5.30 pm on October 11 that Khan had been admitted to a hospital with gunshot injuries. He was subsequently declared dead. A case was registered at Ranhola police station, and an investigation was launched. Police said they had identified the suspects and were making efforts to apprehend them. The motive behind the killing and the circumstances leading to the shooting have not yet been established. Further investigation is underway, police said. (With Agency Inputs)

End of Article
